analysis: Documentation-only changes. docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md head line 689 updates the gpt-oss-20b checkpoint size row: K/V now described as bf16 on all 24 layers (3.15 MB window, 25.17 MB per 1,024 tokens, 154.1 MB file at 6,144) instead of float32 on 23 of 24 layers. docs/reference/configuration.md line 3 updates the date, and line 593 adds a note that bf16 GPT-OSS keeps bf16 activations, so MLX_QUANTIZED_CONSTANT_CACHE does not apply. Neither change alters cache gating (PrefixCachePolicy.isEnabled, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE semantics), TTL, disk budget, HMAC name derivation, DBK3 AAD, cacheSalt scoping or staging-release paths, which are the T-041 detection_hint review triggers. Smaller per-checkpoint files modestly reduce at-rest volume and staging cost; they do not change the kind of exposure (T-041/SEC-035 unchanged). The doc implies storage identity binds per-layer dtype (head lines 427-431). If the underlying code changed the GPT-OSS KV dtype, a dtype change should alter the storage identity and namespace so old float32 files are not misinterpreted. That code is not in this batch and was not verified here; integration should confirm that any related source change keeps dtype in CompleteCheckpointStorageIdentity. No security regression was identified in the supplied units.
